payload.summary: Six Australian and WA publishers are unregistered, so eight Australian sources cannot enter the ledger at all while 14 UK NICE guidelines can
payload.detail: src/lib/source-authority-registry.ts does not contain Centre for Clinical Interventions (a WA Health service), Phoenix Australia (issuer of the national PTSD guidelines), Australasian ADHD Professionals Association, COPE Centre of Perinatal Excellence, Australian Government Department of Health Disability and Ageing, or Monash University. acquisitionLedgerIssues rejects any record whose publisher the register cannot place in a jurisdiction, so eight reconciled Therapy sources are held entirely and can never leave D band. The register meanwhile admits the 14 NICE guidelines registered on 2026-09-16, which inverts the WA-first order docs/source-acquisition-protocol.md requires. MEASURED 2026-09-16, and this changes the priority: registering all six admits ZERO usable sources. Every one of the eight also fails on a missing publication date, which the protocol forbids inferring, so each would enter as a rejection rather than a candidate. The register is a gate but not the binding one. Registering a publisher is also a retrieval-selection change: the chain is classifySourceAuthority to australianSourceTier to selectAustralianClinicalContext, and pr-policy lists source-authority-registry.ts as a RAG-ranking protected surface, so it needs an eval canary. Offline blast radius measured at two dictionary catalogue entries, both band D before and after. Owner decided on 2026-09-16 to hold the registration and pursue publication dates instead. Next action: chase dates for the eight blocked sources by reading the documents themselves, as was done successfully for the WA Aboriginal Health Impact Statement policy; revisit registration only if a dated edition makes a source admissible.
